title: Surge-smoothing hostside token shedder and IO coordinator
creator: Ava Morales
description: Intermittent request bursts cause host-side CPU/GPU pipeline thrashing: large numbers of prefill requests arrive, causing redundant memcpy spikes, threadpool contention, and suboptimal kernel switching on the GPU. This ticket implements a hostside surge-smoothing component (token shedder + IO coordinator) to reduce memcopy storms, stabilize threadpool load, and provide kernel-selection hints to the runtime so the GPU can avoid frequent kernel churn.
background: Recent production incidents and lab repros showed latency P95 increases during sudden traffic spikes. Profiling points to three correlated causes: 1) many concurrent prefill memcopies from host to pinned staging buffers creating PCIe bursts and IRQ overloads; 2) threadpool oversubscription where worker threads contend on short-lived locks while waiting for device fences; 3) frequent kernel-type switches (e.g., from default attention to flash-attn to quantized kernels) because batches arriving at different sequence-lengths trigger different kernel selectors, increasing GPU kernel load and dispatch latency.
proposed_solution: Introduce a lightweight Host IO Coordinator process in the runtime host agent that: (a) monitors prefill queue depth and per-request priority metadata; (b) applies a token-shedding policy to low-priority or stale prefill tokens (soft-drop with short retry/backoff); (c) aggregates small prefill memcpy operations into coalesced single-copy windows using per-NUMA staging buffers; (d) emits kernel-hint metadata (preferred kernel family and quantization mode) to the GPU kernel selector to prefer compatible kernels for the next dispatch; (e) adds adaptive threadpool gating to allow worker parking rather than busy-waiting during sustained IO bursts. Implementation will be feature-flagged and telemetry-enabled for comparison with current pipeline.

acceptance_criteria: Baseline reproducible load test: run synthetic burst workload (1k concurrent prefill requests for 10s) and compare: 50% reduction in number of discrete host->GPU memcpy ops per second
P95 tail latency for streaming decode decreases by >= 20% under the burst workload
Threadpool contention events (lock wait histogram) reduced by >= 40% during bursts
No regression in average latency under steady-state traffic (within +/- 5%)
Kernel dispatch churn (number of distinct kernel families dispatched per second) decreases by >= 30% during bursts
Feature flag rollback path validated and automated

Integrate kernel-hint into request envelope and wire to kernel selector
Add adaptive threadpool gating (park/unpark) and queuing strategy
Add telemetry: histograms, counters, and debug traces for memcopy windows
Write unit + integration tests that simulate burst patterns
Create loadtest harness and dashboards comparing control vs experiment
blockers: Finalize kernel selector API for accepting external hints (research team dependency)

Need hardware QA run on quantized kernels with hint compatibility
